Native-order curve research · continuation 04

Local targeting works briefly.
A richer local flow fixes the depth toy.

Static recursive masks do not preserve their initial advantage during continued Pythia training. Separately, a real two-channel construction preserves the depth-dependent routing computation that the previous scalar flow could not represent.

17 October 2026 · Pythia-70m, step143000 · 120 new model updates · 4,000 tiny toy updates · fixed controls, fresh primary evaluation inputs

Measured outcomesMask experimentDepth constructionImplicationsReproduce

What this phase establishes

The useful negative result: the targeted mask beats the random-mask mean by 3.78 percentage points of copying accuracy after one update, but trails it by 9.69 points after 24 updates. At the endpoint it also has higher text NLL (+0.0188). A useful local gradient signal is not a stable update policy.

The mask comparison controls both the number of enabled coefficients within every original tensor/wavelet band and the global size of each optimizer update. Every coefficient remains stored at full resolution. This rules out a simple “the targeted model changed fewer coefficients or took smaller steps” explanation for its difference from the random masks.

Masking updates in complete native-order curves

Each of the 72 decoder tensors is independently flattened in its original C order and represented by its complete orthonormal Haar pyramid: 18,914,304 coefficients in total. Embeddings, final normalization and the output head remain fixed. Float64 master coefficients decode into the ordinary float32 dense network. This tests curve-coordinate training; it does not replace Pythia attention with geometric self attention.

Within each tensor/detail band, consecutive 64-coefficient tiles are scored using two calibration gradients. The adaptation gradient averages the first six adaptation batches. The copying gradient averages 12 batches of fresh labeled copying probes, with one repeated and one scrambled-query sequence per batch. No held-out test is used to choose the mask.

score(tile) = Σi in tile gcopy,i · [−gadapt,i / (|gadapt,i| + 10−8)]

Lower scores predict a more favorable first-order change in copying NLL for a fresh-Adam-style adaptation proposal. The targeted mask allows the lowest-scoring half of tiles; the opposite mask allows the same number of highest-scoring tiles. Two random masks select exactly the same number in every band. Odd tile counts use floor-half. Bands smaller than 128 coefficients remain enabled in all arms.

Each masked arm enables 9,461,760 coefficients (50.024% of the complete representation). The 295,380 scored tiles preserve native locations. A level j coefficient has support 2j original values; a64-coefficient tile spans 64×2j successive values inside its tensor. No neurons, channels or tensor rows are reordered.

Training and control details

All five arms take 24 AdamW updates, learning rate 2×10−5, β=(0.9,0.999), ε=10−8, no weight decay, no dropout and fresh optimizer states. Each sees the same 48 adaptation blocks,4,560 next-token targets, and the same 24 copying/24 text replay examples from the preceding phase. The frozen starting checkpoint supplies the teacher distributions.

L = Ladaptation + ½ (KLcopy + KLtext)

KL is teacher-to-student over the full vocabulary at temperature 1. Copy replay covers all query positions; text replay uses eight fixed prediction positions per block. Gradients on disabled coefficients are set to zero. After Adam forms its masked proposal, the enabled update is scaled to the unrestricted arm’s L2 norm at that update number. Moments are not rescaled. The largest measured norm discrepancy is 4.86e-17; disabled float64 masters remain exactly unchanged.

Matching each step norm does not match cumulative displacement, optimizer direction, or adaptation progress. Dense decoding also means this implementation is not a speed benchmark. The mask-construction method consumes labeled calibration probes; those labels are additional information used by the targeting rule.

What the failure does and does not say

The endpoint rejects this particular static mask as a retention improvement on this run. It does not reject recursive decomposition as a representation or as a source of local targeting information: the immediate held-out intervention shows that the initial signal is useful. A plausible explanation is that the locally useful directions change as the model and Adam state move, but this phase does not directly measure gradient-score aging or prove that refreshing masks will solve it.

Accuracy and target NLL are both included because preserving top-1 choices alone can conceal probability changes. Scrambled-copy probes and the eight reused prose passages are additional diagnostics, not broad semantic coverage. Evaluation rows and synthetic token pools are disjoint from mask selection and replay; WikiText absence from original Pythia pretraining is not established.

A constructive remedy for the depth failure

The previous scalar family used h′(s)=[a(s)I+b(s)S]h, where S shifts each ring site to its successor. Its generators commute, so its continuous flow is exp(AI+BS). That real scalar family cannot equal the six-hop shift S6 on the 12-site ring: unit gain in the zero and Nyquist modes forces A=B=0, leaving identity. The constant discrete oracle is exact at six Euler steps but has continuous-limit expected MSE 0.795814.

Here each site holds two ordinary real numbers, x and y, with y initially zero. Each hop alternates an onsite rotation and a nearest-neighbor rotation:

Onsite:    xᵢ ← cos(a) xᵢ − sin(a) yᵢ
           yᵢ ← sin(a) xᵢ + cos(a) yᵢ

Neighbor:  xᵢ ← cos(b) xᵢ + sin(b) yᵢ₊₁
           yᵢ ← cos(b) yᵢ − sin(b) xᵢ₋₁

All right-hand sides within one rotation use its input state.
At a=b=π/2, the pair maps (x,y) → (Sx,S⁻¹y).
After six pairs: (x,0) → (S⁶x,0).

There is no learned global input/readout shortcut, imposed state manifold or quaternion representation. The two generators do not commute. The construction changes both state capacity and the operator family; this experiment does not identify augmentation alone as the necessary ingredient.

For a continuous depth field, put each of the 12 rotation generators inside a disjoint smooth pulse. On interval j/12≤s≤(j+1)/12, let u=12s−j and amplitude gj(s)=24θjsin²(πu), with zero amplitude outside. The pulse integrates to θj, and its value and first derivative vanish at its boundaries. The generator curve is C1. Each partial pulse has analytic angle θj[F(u₁)−F(u₀)], where F(u)=u−sin(2πu)/(2π).

Exact conversion of this toy operator: six discrete shifts become 12 local quarter-turn pulses. A solver that splits at pulse boundaries and applies each integrated rotation preserves the same operator on every tested grid, including irregular grids 17 and31. This is an explicit construction for this routing map, not a conversion algorithm for arbitrary Transformer layers.

The construction is learnable in this toy

Five seeds train either 12 pulse angles or two angles shared across the six onsite/neighbor pairs. Both use 400 Adam updates at learning rate 0.05, batch 64 independent Gaussian rings, and fixed 12-pulse execution. Stagewise one-through-six-hop targets and zero-auxiliary targets provide training-only supervision. Initialization is Normal(1,0.1), paired across arms; the shared version uses per-type means. All ten runs are retained.

2 shared controls51.36e-31 [1.06e-36, 4.44e-31]1.55e-152.35e-18

Evaluation reconstructs the exact linear operator from 12 impulses, giving expected output MSE for iid unit Gaussian inputs. An independent 4,096-example Gaussian set checks empirical MSE and sign accuracy. All ten learned models preserve their own output across every tested grid to a maximum absolute difference of 1.55e-15. Small residual auxiliary energy is reported separately.

Uniform midpoint rotations miss or misintegrate narrow pulses on some grids. Boundary-aware forward Euler uses the correct integrated pulse areas but still distorts rotations severely at these step sizes. These are solver failures in a family that has an exact representation. The successful exact solver exploits the closed form of this toy; arbitrary learned operators may not have one.

Cost: 12→24 real state values and 6→at least 12 local mixing operations. Irregular grid 17 requires 28 rotations because cells crossing pulse boundaries are split. This demonstrates representability and subdivision consistency, with no claim of equal computation, general adaptive-depth savings or faster inference.

Implications for the curve-space goal

Representation, optimization and execution remain separate questions. Complete curve coordinates preserve an ordinary model’s stored function at conversion. Subsequent optimization can damage behavior even when every coefficient is retained; this phase adds a controlled example where a locally helpful mask becomes harmful over 24 updates. Changing the execution operator can also remove functions the original model used, as the prior scalar flow did.

The new construction shows that such a failure need not be fundamental to continuous curves. A richer real-state operator with noncommuting local actions can preserve the missing routing function under subdivision. It does not establish equivalence between the user’s GSA architecture and Pythia, or show that any specific pretrained language capability survives that architectural conversion.

The next targeted question is whether feedback can maintain useful update directions: recompute masks on separate calibration data, compare with masks frozen for the same total update budget, and evaluate teacher-distribution preservation rather than only copying-label gradients. The depth counterpart is to test richer operators with state-dependent actions and approximate solvers while charging their actual operation count. Neither improvement is assumed from the current evidence.

Relationship to prior work

Orthogonal Gradient Descent (Farajtabar et al., 2020) motivates constraining updates to limit interference. Our static wavelet-tile masks are a different method and do not reproduce its projection guarantees. Augmented Neural ODEs (Dupont et al., 2019) studies how adding state dimensions can enlarge continuous-flow expressivity. The explicit ring construction and solver comparison here are our own small derivation and experiment.

The original project archive uses recurrent bank coordinates and token-conditioned curve fields. Those coordinates are not equated with layer depth here. No full reproduction of the proposed GSA architecture is claimed.

Checks, provenance and reproduction

The successful Pythia experiment took 359.2s with three CPU threads; the toy took 7.7s with one thread. This excludes source preparation, analysis, figures, checkpoint reloads and an initial calibration-only attempt. That first attempt stopped before any training/evaluation when a QKV band had an odd number of 64-coefficient tiles. The floor-half rule was clarified before rerunning; details are preserved in execution_notes.json.

Both prespecified saved Pythia checkpoints were reloaded and all evaluated text/copy/prose metrics reproduced with maximum difference 0.00e+00. All per-band mask counts, step norms, frozen masters and 80 learned toy/grid measurements passed their checks. This is bounded verification of the reported experiment, not a claim of universal correctness.
